item.title: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem, restores free trade deal with Israel
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday, becoming the 10th country to do so, as new President Abelardo de la Espriella reversed his predecessor's break with Israel by also restoring a free trade agreement between the two countries.

• Most countries maintain their embassies to Israel in Tel Aviv. Israel regards Jerusalem as its capital, while Palestinians seek East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent state. The city's status remains one of the most contentious issues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
item.description:
By Timour Azhari, Jana Choukeir and Tala Ramadan

RIYADH, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia and said they struck the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco, which was hit the day before.

The Iran-aligned group said it had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities inthe eastern city of Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, without saying when.

item.title: IMF calls for US to cut deficits amid bond woes, China to shift away from exports
item.description:
By David Lawder

BANGKOK, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt without tax or spending adjustments, while China must pivot from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday.

item.title: Yemen fighting overwhelms hospitals, cuts aid to 800,000 people, relief agencies say
item.description:
By Olivia Le Poidevin

GENEVA, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties, while intensified fighting along multiple front lines has cut off aid to around 800,000 people, humanitarian agencies said on Wednesday.

Front-line hospitals in areas including Marib, Taiz and Yemen's Red Sea coast are seeing unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients, with some facilities admitting more than 700 casualties in a single week, according to the Red Cross.

item.title: Gazans harvest dregs of olive groves bulldozed and cut off by Israel
item.description:
By Mahmoud Issa and Nidal al-Mughrabi

GAZA/CAIRO, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Haidar Abu Middain, 60, lifts a desiccated bough of a fallen olive tree and tosses it aside in the barren dirt of what was once one of the most prosperous groves in central Gaza.

The family olive orchard he owned with his brothers and his uncles used to span 900 dunums — 220 acres — of trees that this time of year would be heavy with ripe fruit.

item.title: U.S.-Russia deal on diesel is 'very risky choice,' Italy PM Meloni says
item.description:
By Giuseppe Fonte

ROME, Oct 14 (Reuters) - The deal between the United States and Russia over diesel supply is a "very risky choice" that runs counter to efforts to force Vladimir Putin to sit at a negotiating table with Ukraine, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Wednesday.

The United States and Russia agreed last week that Moscow would initially supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to U.S. and ​global markets.

item.title: Barbados joins push for global panel to tackle inequality
item.description:
By Rae Wee

BANGKOK, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Barbados is joining a group of countries calling for the establishment of an international panel to address inequality, at a time when heightened geopolitical tensions, climate change and rapid technological advances threaten to widen the divide between wealthy and poorer nations.

Policymakers from developing economies are increasingly sounding the alarm over the impact ofmounting debt burdens, rising food and fuel costs, and the risk of being left behind in the AI investment boom.

item.title: Kamala Harris warns window closing for AI safeguards, urges US-China cooperation
item.description:
By Kyu-seok Shim

SEOUL, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Former US Vice President Kamala Harris urged governments and technology companies on Wednesday to urgently put safeguards in place for artificial intelligence, warning that the window for containing its gravest risks was closing.

"If we are to have any guardrails and safeguards, they have to be at the table," Harris said of AI developers during an appearance at South Korea's Asan Institute for Policy Studies.

"My concern is that the window is shutting."

item.title: Seeing pivotal election, Israelis fly from around world to vote
item.description:
Liran Naaman said he spent 800 euros (nearly $900) to fly from Amsterdam, where he has lived for the past 11 years, to his native Israel, all to vote in the October 27 election.

He has returned to vote in every election except during the Covid-19 pandemic, and believes this time his participation matters more than ever. "The way that our government is conducting itself is harming me personally and the rest of the Israelis abroad," the project manager told AFP.

item.title: Regulator 'will resign' if any political interference in Man City case
item.description:
The chair of English football's Independent Regulator has said he will resign if there is political interference in any future investigation into Manchester City as a result of widespread impropriety. 

City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict.

item.title: Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
item.description:
By Parisa Hafezi, Jonathan Saul and Phil Stewart

DUBAI/LONDON/WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.

item.title: Saudi employee arrested for allegedly bugging OpenAI office
item.description:
A Saudi employee of OpenAI was arrested after allegedly planting a recording device in one of the company's San Francisco offices, the AI firm and federal prosecutors said Tuesday.

"We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices" and "referred the matter to the FBI," OpenAI told AFP in a statement.

OpenAI's security team found the device late last month and the employee, Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on October 9, the US Justice Department said.

item.title: Southern Yemeni leader calls for 'mobilization’ against Houthis as war escalates
item.description: Aidarous al-Zubaidi, who leads the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council separatist group, called on southern Yemenis to fight for regional autonomy and against the Houthis, while condemning attacks on Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Saudi Aramco headquarters attacked, limited fire reported
item.description:
By Timour Azhari, Maha El Dahan and Menna AlaaElDin

RIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The headquartersof Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked on Tuesday night, causing what the kingdom's energy ministry said in a statement was a limited fire, as fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified.

Authorities responded to the incident in an administrative building at the headquarters complexlate on Tuesday and took necessary measures, the ministry said, adding that there were no injuries or deaths.

item.title: Iran mum as Azerbaijan’s school hijab ban, Israel ties test alliance with Turkey
item.description: Azerbaijan’s restrictions on Islamic dress in schools have sparked an unusual public spat with Turkey, exposing tensions beneath the allies’ close political and security ties.
